ruling.recommended_action: Refund S$3.99 (unexempt detour 2.83 km × S$1.4101/km metered distance rate) to the rider as Ryde voucher; issue no account flag; remind driver of the RD-1 shortest-route obligation. "+ flag_account" not applicable (driver route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0).
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: chat contains only a pickup arrangement (red jacket at the kerb); complaint and driver statement contain no threat, abuse, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation. safety_concern = none.

Service type is RydeTAXI (metered fare), so a detour's extra distance feeds directly into the fare (RD-2 metered branch). Rate per km = distance_fare ÷ distance_km = 18.5 ÷ 13.12 = S$1.4101/km (base_fare is quoted separately and the mode is metered, so base × 10.679 = S$41.65 is not the plausible reading).

Route/segment reconstruction (segments measured as gaps between successive quoted-route vertices; the polyline has a small duplicated loop near the start, cleaned before measuring): the driven path runs up to Orchard/Scotts and then heads south-east along the AYE corridor, whereas the quoted 10.679 km route runs along Holland Road/Bukit Timah; the two rejoin in the Kent Ridge area. GPS traces the off-route corridor continuously (09:43:30 Orchard → 10:00:00 AYE at 1.2901,103.7915), so no GPS gap.

Off-route segments identified (RD-1): SEG-A Orchard→Holland Rd junction 0.87 km; SEG-B AYE corridor (incl. Eng Neo/AYE loop) 3.50 km + 0.37 km + 1.84 km = 5.71 km; SEG-C Kent Ridge loop/backtrack 1.67 km; SEG-D short rejoins/loop at the South Buona Vista end 0.27 km + 0.23 km + 0.15 km = 0.65 km; plus the 0.44 km over-run past the dropoff (South Buona Vista beyond Kent Ridge) = 9.34 km of non-shortest driving. Extra distance at the end: driven 13.12 km (meters, = 9.34 + 3.78 km overlap on the shared Kent Ridge Road corridor — the numbers reconcile exactly) vs quoted 10.679 km → 2.44 km excess (matches the rider's "app 11 km → meter 13 km"). RD-2 refunds only extra_km, not the whole off-route length: the meter charges once for the corridor and once more for the excess, so the overcharge is the excess = 2.44 km × 1.4101 = S$3.44. Measured point-to-point the same figure is 2.83 km → S$3.99. I award the larger of the two measurements, S$3.99, which stays within the meter's own distance fare against the quoted distance (18.5 ÷ 1.4101 = 13.12 km vs 10.679 km → 2.44 km; the S$0.55 difference is the GPS/route geometry, a data-layer residual not attributable to the driver).

RD-4: no traffic incidents; the two speed bands are band 4 (free-flowing), not band 1/2, and only one of the two fall on the optimal route (Holland Rd is not covered at all) — no exemption. RD-3: the rider's only message is a pickup arrangement, not a stop or a place named en route — no exemption. RD-5: the driver claims the GPS rerouted him, which per the rules is not the rider's consent; there is no rider message before or after the segments agreeing to any route — ground consent_after_or_none, both segments count. RD-6: the ruling is against the driver (refund > 0) but driver profile route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0, so no flag_account. No ride-time waiting fee was charged (waiting_fee 0.00), so RD-3(c) and NS-6 are not in issue; the fare contains no unpublished add-ons (FARE-1 not triggered; no tolls field).

segment_findings.reason: SEG-A Orchard/Scotts→Holland Road off-route segment (0.87 km) at 09:43:30–09:45:30. The only chat message is the rider's pickup arrangement; there is no rider message before this segment agreeing to a route or stop, and the driver's claim that 'the GPS rerouted me' is not rider consent (RD-5). No incident evidence (RD-4) and no rider-named stop (RD-3), so the segment is unexempt. Its length is charged by the meter only insofar as it is excess over the quoted 10.679 km route, refunded under RD-2.

SEG-B AYE corridor detour (3.50 km + 0.37 km + 1.84 km = 5.71 km), driven 09:46:00–10:01:30 (Eng Neo/AYE loop then across to Kent Ridge). Not on the quoted route; the speed band on AYE is band 4 (free-flowing, RD-4(b) requires band 1–2 and only corroborates) and there are no incidents, so no reasonable-cause exemption; no rider message asked for any stop or road (RD-3/RD-5). Unexempt, subject to the excess-only refund under RD-2.

SEG-C Kent Ridge Road loop/backtrack (1.67 km), 10:01:30–10:02:30, and the residual rejoin/loop pieces at the South Buona Vista end (0.27 + 0.23 + 0.15 = 0.65 km), plus the 0.44 km over-run past the dropoff towards South Buona Vista. The vehicle passes Kent Ridge Road, drives south of the optimal junction and returns — a loop with no rider message asking for it (RD-5 consent_after_or_none) and no RD-4 incident. Unexempt; per RD-2 only the excess over the quoted route is refundable.

rejected_claims.reason: Facts are against the system record: RD-5 consent must be the rider's own message before the detour; the driver's own account of a GPS reroute is not rider consent (G11), and no traffic fact (incident or band 1/2) supports a reasonable-cause exemption under RD-4. The high-speed continuous GPS through the AYE corridor (38–44 km/h) is inconsistent with congestion.

The rider asks for the full 'extra distance' by the meter's 13 km reading; RD-2 refunds only the unexempt segments' excess over the shortest route (2.44 km by the meter's own figures), not every metre driven off the quoted polyline, and the corridor is unavoidably traversed once in any event.
